s.g: (intransitive, transitive, stative, Internet slang, originally incel slang) To manifest effortless dominance through self-evident superior handsomeness, especially with composure and by quiet comparison.
s.x: He mogged him just by standing next to him.

s.g: (transitive, stative, by extension, Internet slang) To be superior to (something); to beat, outclass.
(intransitive, US, UK, dialectal) To move or walk slowly; to trudge, amble; (more broadly) to go.
(transitive, intransitive) In the game of costly colours: to exchange (a card) with the dealer.
(transitive, US, UK, dialectal, rare) To cause to move; to drive.
(UK, colloquial) A cat.
s.x: Get that mog out of here!

s.g: (transitive, Australia, informal) To remove (a public servant) from their position following a Machinery of Government change, a process in which the Government of Australia reorganizes the responsibilities and structure of the government.
(Canada, Newfoundland) A traditional soft cookie made with molasses, spices, dried fruits, and toasted pecans.
s.x: Nan made a batch of fresh mogs for Christmas—rich with molasses and full of raisins.

moga.f: Alternative form of muga (“type of silk”).

s.g: (obsolete) A high-grade animal skin from this region.
(aviation) Automotive gasoline suitable for use in some piston-engined gasoline powered aircraft.
(slang) The drug nitrazepam (Mogadon).

(Yorkshire) A kind of cake made with ginger, treacle, etc.
(Scotland and Northern England regional, obsolete) Synonym of girl: a female child or young woman.
(Midlands and Northern England regional, derogatory, rare) Synonym of slattern: an unkempt or badly-dressed woman.
(Midlands and Northern England regional, rare) Synonym of scarecrow.
(South Africa, Zimbabwe, slang) Irrational, out of touch.

(Africa) cassava
